content: 1. The metabolism of valbenazine is influenced by CYP3A4. When co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, the dose of valbenazine should be reduced, and therapy should be closely monitored. 2. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The starting dose of vamorolone should be reduced to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 3. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The dose of vardenafil may need to be reduced when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 4. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 5. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 6. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor during the initiation and ramp-up phase in patients with CLL/SLL is contraindicated. For patients on a steady daily dose after the ramp-up phase, consider adjusting the venetoclax dosage and closely monitor for adverse reactions. In AML patients, adjust the venetoclax dosage and monitor closely. Resume the pre-inhibitor venetoclax dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A inhibitor. 7. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 8. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of verapamil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 9. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 10. Chloramphenicol increases the levels of vilazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 11. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 12. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vincristine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 13. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 14. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 15. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated. 16. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the serious risk. 17. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of warfarin by mechanisms involving other pathways. Warfarin's less potent R-enantiomer is partially metabolized by CYP3A4 (as well as CYP1A2 and CYP2C19). Monitor INR more frequently if co-administered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 18. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 19. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the zolpidem dose when co-administered with a CYP3A4 inhibitor. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 20. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy closely. 21. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 22. Chloramphenicol has been associated with serious and potentially fatal blood dyscrasias, including aplastic anemia, hypoplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and granulocytopenia, which can occur after both short-term and prolonged therapy. Monitor complete blood counts (CBC) frequently in all patients. 23. Use chloramphenicol only for serious infections. Avoid repeated courses of treatment if possible, and do not continue therapy longer than necessary to cure the disease with minimal risk of relapse. 24. Impaired liver or kidney function may lead to excessive blood levels of chloramphenicol at recommended doses. Adjust the dosage accordingly and preferably determine blood concentrations at appropriate intervals. 25. The use of antibiotics, including chloramphenicol, may result in the overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms, including fungi. Take appropriate measures if such organisms appear during therapy. 26. Gray syndrome has been reported in premature infants and neonates. It is characterized by abdominal distension (with or without emesis), progressive pallid cyanosis, vasomotor collapse often accompanied by irregular respiration, and death within hours of symptom onset. It may be associated with serum levels exceeding 50 mcg/mL after repeated doses. 27. Chloramphenicol is classified as Pregnancy Category C. It enters breast milk; discontinue the drug or avoid nursing. 28. Administer chloramphenicol via direct IV infusion over 3-5 minutes or intermittent infusion over 30-60 minutes. 29. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
